page_placements.theme: What sets the amount of compensation: training data, objective, pretraining stage, width/scale, training under a lesion

record.file_problem: The text is complete, but some mathematical expressions are missing or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports lesion-induced recovery after supervised fine-tuning, not within-forward-pass compensation by later components. The recovery was deliberately induced by training under the lesion, so it does not test the claim as specified.
record.gate_note: The reported task-accuracy recovery, fresh-lens evaluation, residual perturbation measurements, and CKA results concern adaptation to a lesion during fine-tuning. They do not measure the versions' specified layer/head self-repair, late-MLP counterbalancing, named mechanisms, on-distribution ablation comparison, or attribution effects. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains Qwen3.5-4B with a J-lens-direction lesion active during SFT and measures recovery of task accuracy after training. That recovery is deliberately induced by training, not compensation by later components within a forward pass. No single layer or head is ablated. The Hydra Effect and Explorations of Self-Repair appear only in Related Work. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors add that training did not make the lesion weaker (norm removal is similar until the last block), so recovery likely came from elsewhere. CKA shows internal geometry changed, but no mechanism is identified. They call this early evidence of lesion-induced functional compensation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a model with a sequential, top-10 J-lens-direction residual intervention active at six blocks; it does not reproduce single-layer or single-head ablation self-repair measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention magnitude varies across blocks; the early-to-late CKA relationship differs between clean, lesioned, and trained conditions. The primary and second-seed task results also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: SFT with a J-direction lesion active throughout training restores task accuracy under the lesion: 20.9% before training, 97.7% (primary seed) and 92.2% (second seed) after. Recovery persists under a freshly fitted lens (124/129).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A model fine-tuned under a persistent activation lesion can learn to maintain task performance despite the lesion.

fits_no_version.finding: Ordinary SFT and matched-random-perturbation training also improve accuracy under the J-lesion, but less than training under the lesion itself.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic training partly increases tolerance to a J-direction lesion; training under the lesion yields much greater recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: After training, the lesion still removes a similar residual-stream norm, and the CKA geometry between early and late layers shifts (0.72 clean, 0.77 lesioned, 0.57 after recovery).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recovery after lesion-constrained training coexists with persistent residual perturbation and reorganised layer geometry.

record.problems: The study is a single-model demonstration due to compute constraints. Its selected cohort and hyperparameter/duration selection limit generalization; the reported intervals do not account for task selection, hyperparameter selection, or uncertainty across model families. Fresh-lens fitting did not include the original paper's full lens-quality validation suite. The results concern recovery deliberately induced by supervised fine-tuning, not spontaneous within-forward-pass self-repair.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were omitted. Legacy experiments are described as exploratory and not reproduced on the corrected models, so they were not recorded as current results.

untested.parts: No single attention layer is ablated; no compensation by later layers within a forward pass is measured.
No late-MLP downregulation of the top token, and no change in erasure after ablation, is measured.
No head ablations; no full-distribution measurement across model families or sizes.
No within-forward-pass compensation fraction, per-prompt variance or overcorrection is measured.
No backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons are examined.
No comparison of zero, mean or resample ablation.
No ablation-based importance scores are compared with direct or total effects.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the self-repair papers appear only in Related Work. Norm-ratio values in r12/r13 (0.779/0.835) come from the fresh-lens Appendix A2. The main text gives about 78%/84% and attributes them to the published lens.

versions.untested_parts: No single attention layer is ablated and no later attention-layer compensation within a forward pass is measured.
No late MLP counterbalancing, maximum-likelihood-token downregulation, or change in erasure after earlier-component ablation is measured.
No single attention heads are ablated and no full-distribution self-repair across general text, model families, or sizes is tested.
The study does not measure prompt-level variability or overcorrection in within-forward-pass self-repair.
The study does not test backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as mechanisms.
It does not compare mean or resample ablations with zero ablation. Its J-direction lesion is applied during supervised fine-tuning.
No ablation-based importance score is compared with a component's direct or total effect.

relation.reason: The Hydra Effect and Explorations of Self-Repair appear as Related Work links without substantive discussion, testing, or use of their findings.

tranche.reason: Recovery is deliberately induced through supervised training with a persistent residual-stream lesion. The study does not measure spontaneous compensation within a forward pass or test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The 129-example headline cohort combines validation and screen examples; validation selected learning rate and duration. Recovery after training does not establish a self-repair mechanism; the author leaves representation changes, rerouting, and reduced intervention effects unresolved.
